title: Hand of Two
user: Couples and friends who want a quick, replayable two-player tactical card game without buying a collectible deck or learning a 40-minute ruleset.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN poster asks for favorite two-person card games after enjoying German Whist and Cribbage with their spouse.
A 151-score, 75-comment co-op request seeks games for two or more people that are actually fun with little to no internet, specifically to prepare in advance.

recurrence: Separate two-player and low-connectivity threads, with 75 responses in the latter, show a recurring desire for compact social play outside a large online service.
current_workaround: Learn traditional card games, buy a physical deck, install a multiplayer client, or send links to heavyweight digital card games.
incumbents_and_gap: Cribbage, German Whist, Cuttle, and Board Game Arena offer card play, but are either physical, need accounts/large rulesets, or present a broad platform rather than an immediate 12-minute duel.
smallest_useful_product: A room-code, two-player browser card duel with a fixed 18-card shared deck. Players draft three weather cards, play six simultaneous turns to protect or disrupt a tiny expedition, and reveal a short story epilogue. Each run changes the card mix and map modifier. Inputs are mouse/touch; a game takes 10–15 minutes. Non-goals: collectible cards, ranked ladder, purchases of power, and spectator chat.
success_measure: At least 30% of first rooms immediately start a rematch and median completed match time stays between 8 and 16 minutes.
monetization: one-time — a complete tactical deck and future scenario packs are legible purchases without turning the game into a CCG.
constraints: Use server-authoritative simultaneous resolution to prevent easy room-code cheating; support reconnect within one turn; all art and text must be original and avoid trading-card IP.
why_distinct: It is a finite, original micro-duel about shared prediction, not a browser port of an established card game or a collectible economy.
